title: Fantasy Thought Experiments: Wizards, Castles and Dragons
length_note: Ten classes. The five subjects Mike asked for need different amounts of room. Medieval life and castles get two classes, because village life has to come before castle design. Myths get two, one for dragons and one for wizards. Worldbuilding and map-making get one. The magic market gets one. The science a wizard would need gets two, one on bodies and flight and one on energy and chemistry, because each is a full idea on its own. One opening class teaches the 'what if' method and how we label real versus invented. One closing class lets learners build their own experiment, including a science-fiction version. Classes run 20 to 35 minutes. Each has one main idea and a short recap, so it suits teenagers, adults, and people relearning after a brain injury. Each class can be paused and resumed. Classes 2 to 9 are marked as needing research, so the real history, myth and science are checked against sources before lessons are written. The setting is Nimrod's own medieval village, with no franchise worlds. Every lesson marks each part as REAL (history or science), LEGEND (old stories) or INVENTED (Nimrod).

classes.title: What If? How a Thought Experiment Works
classes.goal: Learner can state a 'what if' question, list the rules they are assuming, and say which parts are real and which are invented.
topics: A thought experiment means asking 'what if' and following the logic step by step
Meet Nimrod's village and its characters: King Kenny, Queen Rose, Jack, Robin the Joker, Princess Jess, Prince Vince, Nimrod the cat, Merlin, Sir Michael, Dame Gladys
The labels used in every class: REAL, LEGEND, INVENTED
Fantasy and science fiction use the same method, and a short example of each
A simple routine: question, assumptions, consequences, what we learned

classes.title: Life in a Medieval Village
classes.goal: Learner can describe how ordinary people in medieval Europe lived and worked, and place Jack, Robin and Dame Gladys in that picture.
topics: REAL: farming year, food, housing, and common jobs in medieval Europe
REAL: who held power and who owed what to whom (the lord and the people who worked the land)
REAL: where our picture of 'the Middle Ages' is too simple, and what historians still debate
INVENTED: what Jack, Robin the Joker and Dame Gladys would do each day in Nimrod village
Thought experiment: what happens to the village if one harvest fails?

classes.title: Inside the Castle
classes.goal: Learner can explain why castles were built the way they were and design a simple castle for King Kenny and Queen Rose.
topics: REAL: why castles were built, and how their main parts worked (walls, gate, keep, moat)
REAL: how castles changed over time, and that they were homes and offices as well as forts
REAL: what knights did, and the difference between a knight and a lord
INVENTED: Nimrod's castle, with Sir Michael as its defender and Princess Jess and Prince Vince growing up there
Thought experiment: where would you put the weak point, and why?

classes.title: Where Dragons Come From: The Myths
classes.goal: Learner can name several real dragon legends from different cultures and say what we do and do not know about why people told them.
topics: LEGEND: dragon and serpent stories from different parts of the world, and how they differ
REAL: how the meaning of dragons changed over time in European stories
REAL but debated: theories that fossils or real animals inspired some dragon stories, and how strong the evidence is
INVENTED: the dragon of Nimrod, with a history built from the real patterns above
Thought experiment: what would a village do if a dragon were a neighbour?

classes.title: Where Wizards Come From: Merlin and the Real Past
classes.goal: Learner can separate the legend of Merlin from real history, and describe the real people behind the idea of a wizard.
topics: LEGEND: where the Merlin stories come from and how they grew over time
REAL: medieval healers, astrologers, alchemists and scholars, and what they actually did
REAL: how people in the past thought about magic, religion and science, and how those ideas overlapped
INVENTED: Nimrod's Merlin and how he fits the village
Thought experiment: how would villagers tell a wizard from a clever scholar?

classes.title: Building a World: Maps and Worldbuilding
classes.goal: Learner can draw a simple map of Nimrod's village and region, and explain how geography shapes who lives where and what they do.
topics: REAL: how medieval people made and used maps, and how they differ from modern maps
REAL: why towns grow where they do (rivers, roads, hills, fields)
Map basics: scale, key, compass, and what to leave out
Worldbuilding rules: keep it consistent, and let one change cause the next
INVENTED: draw Nimrod's map, placing the castle, village, market, and the dragon's home
Thought experiment: move the river, and see what else changes

classes.title: The Magic Market: Economics with Spells
classes.goal: Learner can use ideas such as scarcity, supply and demand, and inflation to predict what happens to prices if magic is added to a market.
topics: REAL: how medieval markets, money and trade worked, at a plain-language level
REAL: basic economic ideas (scarcity, supply and demand, inflation, trade-offs) explained with everyday examples
INVENTED: Robin the Joker sells spells and potions, and Dame Gladys sells bread
Thought experiment 1: what if a wizard could make gold? Why might that make gold less valuable?
Thought experiment 2: what if a spell makes bread plentiful? Who gains and who loses?
Rules for a fair magic economy

classes.title: Science of a Dragon: Size, Flight and Fire
classes.goal: Learner can use real science to say what would make a giant flying, fire-breathing animal hard or easy, and propose a believable fix.
topics: REAL: how animals and birds fly, and how body size limits flight
REAL: why bigger animals need stronger bones and more food
REAL: what 'breathing fire' would need (a fuel, an ignition, and a safe place to store it), with examples of real animals that make chemical defences
INVENTED: the Nimrod dragon's body, redesigned to follow these rules
Thought experiment: how much food would the dragon need, and what would that do to the village?

classes.title: Science of a Wizard: Energy, Chemistry and Evidence
classes.goal: Learner can explain, using real science, what a spell would cost in energy, and how Merlin could test a claim like a scientist.
topics: REAL: energy is never made from nothing, only changed from one form to another
REAL: basic chemistry and what early alchemists got wrong and right
REAL: how a good test works (a fair comparison, repeating results, and checking for tricks)
INVENTED: Merlin's rules for spells, with an energy 'cost' that fits the science
Thought experiment: Merlin lights a lamp with a spell. Where did the energy come from?

classes.title: Your Own Thought Experiment: Fantasy and Science Fiction
classes.goal: Learner can build, test and explain an original 'what if' set in Nimrod, and re-tell it as science fiction.
topics: Pick a question from any earlier class, such as 'what if Prince Vince could talk to the dragon?'
List the assumptions and the likely consequences, and mark each part REAL, LEGEND or INVENTED
Re-skin the idea as science fiction: the wizard becomes an engineer, the dragon becomes an alien animal, the castle becomes a station
Share and give kind, useful feedback
Course recap, and where to go next
